## Learning objectives

::: {.callout-note title="Learning objectives"}
- Execute a real end-to-end Sandcastle path that exercises the five
  construction-layer concerns from
  [Sandcastle · Part 1 · Lesson 1](../../courses/sandcastle/part-1/01-inside-a-sandcastle/index.html):
  isolated workspace, repo/branch flow, tools and permissions, agent
  iteration, and artifact boundary.
- Observe an engineering agent's inner iteration loop (inspect →
  generate → validate → commit) running inside a scoped workspace
  with a PATH allowlist.
- Confirm that only the committed branch survives the workspace
  teardown, and that the same branch — cloned back out afresh —
  still produces a working `hello-world-pico` when passed through the
  reference `pico` CLI.
:::

## Prerequisites

::: {.callout-note title="Prerequisites"}
- Completion of the [Hello Pico lab](../hello-pico/) — this lab
  produces the same `hello-world-pico` artifact, but under a
  Sandcastle instead of by hand.
- Completion of the
  [Sandcastle · Part 1 · Exercise](../../courses/sandcastle/part-1/01-inside-a-sandcastle/exercise.html)
  is recommended — the blueprint you wrote there matches the shape
  of [`downloads/blueprint.yaml`](downloads/blueprint.yaml).
- A working shell (`bash` or `zsh`).
- **`git` 2.30+** and **`python3` 3.8+** on your `PATH`.
- A local clone of this repository, which ships the reference `pico`
  CLI under `bin/pico`.
:::

## Environment

- **Supported OS:** macOS, Linux, or WSL.
- **Required shell:** `bash` 3.2+ or `zsh` 5+.
- **Required tools:**
  - `bash` (POSIX shell) — invoked by the driver and by
    `./build/hello-world-pico`.
  - `git` **2.30+** — clones the local target repo, commits on the
    branch, and pushes it back.
  - `python3` **3.8+** — used by the driver to read the blueprint
    fields and by `bin/pico`.
  - `pico` (this repository's reference CLI, shipped under
    `bin/pico`) — parses `rules/*.yaml` and composes the
    `hello-world-pico` artifact.
- **PATH expectation:** after one-time setup, `command -v pico`
  resolves to `<repo>/bin/pico` (not `/usr/bin/pico`, which is the
  Alpine/nano text editor). `git` and `python3` resolve to their
  standard system paths.
- **Estimated time:** 45–60 minutes.
- **No cluster, container, or network access is required.** The
  entire lab runs against a local target repo under `work/`.

## One-time setup

From a fresh shell, in a local clone of the academy source
repository, put its `bin/` directory on your `PATH`:

```bash
export PATH="$PWD/bin:$PATH"
command -v pico   # should print .../bin/pico
```

The `PATH` export lasts for the current shell session; re-run it in
new shells. This is the same one-time setup used by the
[Hello Pico lab](../hello-pico/objectives.html#one-time-setup).

## Cleanup

The lab writes only inside the repository-ignored `work/` directory.
To remove everything the lab produced:

```bash
rm -rf work/hello-world-pico-sandcastle
```

The `sandcastle-run.sh` driver already deletes its own sandbox
workspace at the end of each run; the command above additionally
removes the seeded local target repo and the captured evidence.
